description: Flow discovery (arXiv 2503.06745). Derives agent execution graphs from trace data and surfaces divergence. KEY CAVEAT: sequence-aware panels (stability score, top-N flows, divergence rate) need per-trace structured logs that include {trace_id, checkpoint}. R13.1's current instrumentation emits checkpoints as span events only — see grafana/recording-rules.md for the small instrumentation change required.

panels.title: Orchestrator -> workers (Jaeger node graph)
panels.description: Live Jaeger trace topology. Edges are spans, nodes are service operations. The orchestrator should fan out to researcher + synthesizer; new edges signal a behavior change.

panels.title: Flow stability score (1h)
panels.description: stability = 1 - (distinct checkpoint kinds / total checkpoint events). A pragmatic Prometheus-only proxy: when the same handful of checkpoints repeat, the score approaches 1.0; when every run introduces new checkpoint names, it heads to 0. Production-grade per-trace-sequence stability is documented as a TODO in recording-rules.md.

panels.title: Mean checkpoints per plan-step (1h)
panels.description: agentops_flow_checkpoints_total / agentops_plan_steps_total. High values suggest agents are firing many checkpoints per plan step — a sign of retry loops or over-planning. Per-agent variant blocked until the flow_checkpoints counter carries an `agent` label (TODO in instrumentation.py:319).

panels.title: Top-N checkpoints by frequency (1h)
panels.description: Each row is a distinct checkpoint name, with how many times agents hit it in the last hour. The spec asked for distinct *sequences*; without per-trace structured logs we can only rank checkpoints. The relative weights here still highlight which checkpoints are load-bearing (the happy-path ones) vs. which are deviation-only (the failure-mode ones like researcher.search_failed).

panels.title: Checkpoint diversity over time
panels.description: Distinct checkpoint names seen per $__interval. Spikes indicate behavior change — agents firing checkpoints they didn't fire before. Approximates 'flow divergence rate'; the true sequence-aware version needs per-trace sequence reconstruction (TODO).

options.content:
**Flow discovery** (arXiv 2503.06745) reframes agent behavior as a process-mining problem: every trace is a *case*, every `flow.checkpoint` span event is an *event*, and the ordered list of checkpoints per trace is a *sequence*. This dashboard derives five things from that:

1. **Node graph** — Jaeger's `dependencyGraph` query, no derivation needed; shows the actual service-call topology.
2. **Flow stability** — `1 - distinct_checkpoint_kinds / total_checkpoint_events`. A Prometheus-only proxy: stays high when the same checkpoints recur, drops when novel checkpoints appear. Range `[0, 1]`. **TODO:** for true per-trace sequence stability, see `grafana/recording-rules.md` Option A — add `trace_id` + `checkpoint` to the agent's structured log line in `instrumentation.py::flow_checkpoint`, and the Loki query reconstructs sequences.
3. **Top-N checkpoints** — `sort_desc(sum by (checkpoint) ...)`. The high-frequency checkpoints are the happy path; long-tail ones are deviation modes (researcher.search_failed, researcher.fetch_failed).
4. **Checkpoint diversity** — distinct-checkpoint count over time. A spike means the agents started doing new things.
5. **Mean checkpoints per plan-step** — total checkpoints divided by total plan-steps. Watches for stuckness (lots of checkpoints per plan).

**Three instrumentation changes** would close the remaining gaps:

- Add an `agent` label to `agentops_flow_checkpoints_total` (one line in `instrumentation.py::flow_checkpoint`).
- Add an `agent` label to `agentops_llm_*` counters (so cost dashboard can attribute spend per agent).
- Log a structured line `{trace_id, agent, checkpoint}` from `flow_checkpoint()` so Loki can do per-trace sequence reconstruction.

title: AgentOps - Flow Discovery
